Definition: from G303 (in the sense of reversal) and G2955; to unbend, i.e. rise; figuratively, be elated:--lift up, look up.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to unbend, to lift yourself up: a woman bound together for eighteen years could in no wise lift up herself, until Jesus laid His hands on her — and Jesus tells His disciples that when these things begin to come to pass, they should look up and lift up their heads, for their redemption draws near. It is the straightening of a bent back, and the lifting of a bowed head.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for lifting up carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the straightening — a woman bent double for eighteen years, and a people told to lift their heads because redemption is near.
